newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea to lift ban on rice supply to North Korea.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea to lift ban on rice supply to North Korea.

text.p: South Korea will lift a ban on private organisations providing rice to impoverished North Korea, a government official said on Monday.
Religious and human rights groups in South Korea are permitted to ship other food aid to the North but Seoul has banned shipments of rice, saying it could be diverted to the military.

"Rice is the most needed grain in North Korea and the government has accepted private organisations' appeals that rice be included in food aid to the North," a government official told Reuters. "A formal announcement will be made later today."

The decision is the latest goodwill gesture by South Korea which is trying to lure the North to four-nation peace talks jointly proposed by U.S. President Bill Clinton and South Korean President Kim Young-sam last April.
The talks, which would include China, are aimed at securing a formal treaty to replace a truce that ended the 1950-53 Korean War, which technically still leaves the two Koreas at war.
Seoul officials said North Korea offered its first formal response to the proposal for talks on Wednesday, demanding substantial food aid at a meeting in New York.
The United States and South Korea insisted there could be no preconditions to the talks but suggested more aid could flow once talks began.
International aid agencies say North Korea, devastated by two consecutive years of floods, is weeks away from famine.
In another gesture of goodwill, a South Korean trade specialist is visiting Pyongyang to pave the way for business ventures.

Hong Ji-seon, who heads the North Korea department at state-run Korea Trade/Investment Promotion Agency, is to arrange a business forum to encourage South Korean businessmen to use North Korea as a processing base for textiles and other labour-intensive manufacturing.
He is due to remain in Pyongyang until Saturday.
Seoul has also agreed to provide $6 million to the latest international food appeal by the World Food Programme (WFP) to North Korea.
The programme says North Korea needs at least 2.3 million tonnes of grain this year.
